subject: Social Media
title: Body Image and Filters
description: A 60-second lesson on Body Image and Filters.

hook.text: A teenager uses a face filter daily. Without it, she doesn't recognize herself. Her real face feels wrong.

buildup.text: Filters reshape faces: thinner nose, bigger eyes, smoother skin. The altered version becomes the expected self.

discovery.text: Plastic surgeons report patients bringing in filtered selfies as goal images. They call it 'Snapchat dysmorphia.'

twist.text: The filters are getting subtler. The new ones don't look like filters—they just make you 'slightly better.'

climax.text: A generation is growing up whose default self-image is a digitally altered face. Real becomes inadequate.

punchline.text: When the filter is the real you, who are you?

quiz.question: What is 'Snapchat dysmorphia'?
options: People seeking plastic surgery to match filtered selfies
